THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT, 1988, AGAOMST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 03.02.2016 PASSED IN MVC.NO.2101/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE MEMBER, ADDITIONL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, HUKKERI, AWARDING COMPENSATIN OF RS.2,56,526/- ALONG WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS REALIZATION.
 THESE APPEALNS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 03.02.2016 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hukkeri, in MVC.no.2101/2013, this appeal and Cross-objection are filed.
2.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hukkeri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts as stated are that on 14.04.2013, claimant was traveling on Jeep bearing registration no.KA-49-8182 from Ghataprabha towards Hukkeri, when driver drove it in rash and negligent manner and caused accident.
In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment at Government Hospital at Hukkeri and Hattaraki Hospital at Gadhinglaj he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
3. Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition against owner and insurer of Jeep under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.

4. Upon service of notice, owner entered appearance and stated that driver was having valid driving licence and vehicle was insured with insurer and sought dismissal of claim petition against himself.
Insurer objected on ground that liability was subject to terms and conditions of policy and there was violation of same.
5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and additional issues and recorded evidence wherein claimant was examined as PW-1 and Dr.S.R.Angadi as PW-2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P21.
In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as RW-1 and owner of vehicle was examined as RW-2.
Exhibits R1 to R4 were marked.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Jeep by its driver and held claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.2,56,256/- from insurer with interest at rate of 6% per annum.

7. Aggrieved by finding of tribunal on liability, insurer is in appeal, while claimant has filed cross- The Manager Shriram General vs Irappa Narayan Badiger on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48647129/
3 objection for enhancement of compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Sri S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel appearing for insurer submitted that as per Ex.P1 - complaint, claimant was traveling on rear footboard of Jeep outside vehicle.
It was further submitted that Exs.R3 and R4 - statement of cleaner and owner of vehicle given in criminal case would indicate that claimant was a fare paid passenger in vehicle.
Since vehicle was insured as private car, carriage of passenger would be in violation of policy conditions.
Therefore, insurer would not be liable.
9. On other hand, Smt. Sunanda A. Patil, learned counsel for claimant - cross-objector submitted that there was no evidence to establish that claimant was traveling as fare paid passenger.

It was further submitted that since vehicle was covered under a private car comprehensive policy, even if contention of insurer were to be tenable, insurer cannot escape liability to pay compensation to claimant, who is a third party.

10. It was also submitted that though claimant was aged 40 years, working as carpenter and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, tribunal considered his monthly income notionally at Rs.6,000/-, which was inadequate.
It was further submitted that tribunal committed error in awarding only Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities and even award towards loss of income during laid up period was inadequate.

It was further submitted that as per deposition of PW-2, implants were inserted,
therefore, tribunal ought to have granted some compensation for removal, under future medical expenses.
11. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and records.
12.
Aggrieved thereby, insurer is in appeal challenging finding on negligence/liability, while claimant is seeking enhancement of compensation.

Therefore, points that arise for consideration are:
"1.
Whether finding of tribunal holding insurer liable to pay compensation calls for interference?
2. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
13. Point no.1: Insofar as liability, from perusal of police investigation records namely Ex.
P1 - complaint given by claimant himself, as well as Ex.P7 - charge sheet
, it is seen that claimant sustained injuries by falling down from jeep, when driver applied brakes suddenly, when he was standing behind vehicle.

As claimant was not traveling inside vehicle, but was standing behind vehicle i.e., outside it on rear footboard, which would be traveling unsafely, he has to be held negligent in contributing in aggravating injuries sustained.
In considered opinion extent of contribution would be 25%.
Thus, insurer cannot be held liable beyond 75%.
Point no.1 is answered accordingly.

4 14.

sentences.text: Point no.2:
In order to establish income, though claimant stated that he was aged 40 years and working as carpenter and earning Rs.10,000/- per month, same was not substantiated.

In absence of specific evidence, tribunal would be justified in taking notional income, but notional income for year 2013 is Rs.7,000/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath.
Therefore, tribunal would not be justified in taking it at Rs.6,000/-.
It would be just and proper to take it at Rs.6,000/-.

In order to establish disability,
claimant produced wound certificates at Exs.P5 and P6 and disability certificate- Ex.P8.
He also examined Dr.S.R.Angadi as PW-2.
From said evidence, it is clear that claimant had sustained grievous injuries and has sustained 45% permanent disability to right lower limb.
Tribunal assessed it at 8%, which would not be adequate.
It would be appropriate to hold it at 15%.

Therefore, future loss of income, by applying multiplier would be '15' as follows:
Rs.7,000/- x 15% x 12 x 15 = Rs.1,89,000/-.
15.

As per PW-2 - Dr.S.R.Angadi, claimant sustained compound fracture of right tibia and fibula,
which was malunited.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to award Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Further, award of Rs.15,000/- towards diet and other incidental charges is sustained.
Likewise award of Rs.33,726/- towards medical expenses against bills produced is also sustained.
Even award of Rs.31,000/- towards pain and suffering is sustained.
Further, normally fractures take three months time to heal.

Therefore, loss of income during laid up period would be:
Rs.7,000/- X 3 = Rs.21,000/-.
16.
In view of finding on point no.1, that claimant sustained aggravated injuries due to his unsafe traveling, claimant would be entitled for only 75% of total award.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative.

. Consequently, following:
O R D E R i. MFA.no.101951/2016 filed by insurer is allowed.
Liability of insurer is limited to 75% of award amount.
ii. MFA.Crob.no.100091/2022 filed by claimant - cross-objector is allowed.
iii. Total compensation is re-
assessed to Rs.3,09,726/- as against Rs.2,56,526/- out of that cross-objector is held entitled to recover 75% award amount from insurer and remaining 25% of award amount from owner.
